newsitem.title: LATVIA: LODE SAYS MAJORITY SHAREHOLDER KEEPS STAKE.
newsitem.headline: LODE SAYS MAJORITY SHAREHOLDER KEEPS STAKE.

text.p: Lode Brick, an active secondary list share, said on Tuesday that its majority shareholder has kept his 49 percent stake denying a newspaper report that it has been sold on the over-the counter market.
Newspaper Diena today noted a large transaction in Lode on the OTC market and said that the company's largest shareholder Edvins Samulis may have sold the shares.
Samulis controlled 502,668 Lode shares in March when blocking his shares ahead of the shareholder meeting.
"This is rubbish as the contolling stake has a block until the privatisation process is completed," Janis Slesars, Lode president, told Reuters.
He said that there had been a misunderstanding with the share accounts.

"Edvins Samulis noticed that these shares were transferred to his account and being an honest person he transferred them back to the depository account where a controlling stake with a block should be held," Slesars said.
"There was a small technical misunderstanding in the bank which services the account," Martinsh Rikshis, president of the central depository, told Reuters.
He said there was a mistake in the statistics, which showed the transfer of shares as a share transaction.
